title: Alligators immersed in helium change their pitch — confirming they use formants to signal body size
description: Chinese alligators vocalising in a helium-enriched atmosphere predictably shifted their dominant frequency upward, while fundamental frequency (controlled by the larynx) was unaffected. This isolates formant resonance as the key channel, proving alligators — like humans — communicate body-size information through vocal-tract resonances. Formant-based signalling predates the mammalian lineage by over 200 million years.
